ns2:section.sectionText: Exercise and Nutrition in Chronic Kidney Disease: Patients with Kidney Failure have exceedingly high mortality rates and a poor quality of life, primarily due to complications associated with cardiovascular disease and muscle wasting. Polypharmacy (excessive prescription of medications) may also paradoxically exacerbate the co-morbid conditions in these patients. Recently, work in our lab and by others indicates that co-morbidities in patients with kidney failure may be better controlled through diet, exercise, and other non-pharmacological strategies. We will discuss the literature related to these topics and also discuss how lessons learned from past failures in the treatment regime for kidney dialysis patients may be relevant to other chronic disease (e.g., diabetes) and aging.
